questions.question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 7(1/5) hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Filling time by pump = 6 hours

Filling time with leakage = 7tfrac{1}{5} hours = tfrac{36}{5} hours

**Formula used:**

Work rate = 1 ÷ Time

Net rate = Filling rate − Leakage rate

**Calculation:**

LCM of 6 and 36/5 = 36

Pump fills = 36 ÷ 6 = 6 units/hour

Net fill = 36 ÷ (36/5) = 5 units/hour

Leak rate = 6 − 5 = 1 unit/hour

Time taken by leak to empty full tank = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 hours

**∴ Leak will empty the full tank in 36 hours.**

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 6 days. If A alone can do it in 7 days, then B alone can do it in ______________ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B = 6 days

A = 7 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM(6,7) units = 42 units

Rate = units per day

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work = 42 units

⇒ (A + B) rate = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 units/day

⇒ A rate = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 units/day

⇒ B rate = 7 - 6 = 1 unit/day

⇒ B time = 42 ÷ 1 = 42 days

**∴ B alone = 42 days.**

questions.question: 3 men and 14 women can complete a piece of work in 18 days, and 11 men and 8 women can complete the same work in 12 days. The work of how many women is equivalent to that of one man?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

3 men and 14 women complete a piece of work in 18 days.

11 men and 8 women complete the same work in 12 days.

Calculation:

Let the work done by 1 man in 1 day = m units.

Let the work done by 1 woman in 1 day = w units.

Total work = Work per day × Number of days.

For 3 men and 14 women:

Work per day = (3 × m) + (14 × w)

Total work = [(3 × m) + (14 × w)] × 18

For 11 men and 8 women:

Work per day = (11 × m) + (8 × w)

Total work = [(11 × m) + (8 × w)] × 12

Since the total work is the same for both groups:

⇒ [(3 × m) + (14 × w)] × 18 = [(11 × m) + (8 × w)] × 12

⇒ 54m + 252w = 132m + 96w

⇒ 132m - 54m = 252w - 96w

⇒ 78m = 156w

⇒ m = 2w

The work of 1 man is equivalent to the work of 2 women.

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 13 days and 52 days, respectively. Both work for 2 days and then A goes away. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A alone = 13 days

B alone = 52 days

Calculations:

Total work = LCM(13,52) = 52 units

⇒ A's efficiency = 52 ÷ 13 = 4 units/day

⇒ B's efficiency = 52 ÷ 52 = 1 unit/day

⇒ (A + B) per day = 4 × 1 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 5 × 2 = 10 units

⇒ Remaining work = 52 − 10 = 42 units

⇒ B alone takes = 42 ÷ 1 = 42 days

**∴ B will take 42 days to complete the remaining work.**

questions.question: Jitesh and Kamal can complete a certain piece of work in 5 and 18 days, respectively, They started to work together, and after 3 days, Kamal left. In how many days will Jitesh complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Jitesh = 5 days, Kamal = 18 days, worked together = 3 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM(5, 18) = 90 units

Efficiency = Total work ÷ Time

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculation:**

⇒ Jitesh’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 units/day

⇒ Kamal’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 units/day

⇒ Together (3 days) = (18 + 5) × 3 = 23 × 3 = 69 units

⇒ Remaining work = 90 − 69 = 21 units

⇒ Time for Jitesh alone = 21 ÷ 18 = 7/6 days

**∴ Jitesh needs 7/6 days.**

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 14 days. If A alone can do it in 63 days, then B alone can do it half of the same work in ______________ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(A + B) finish work in 14 days

A alone finishes in 63 days

Find: Time for B alone to do half of the same work

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work = LCM(14, 63) = 126 units

⇒ (A + B) efficiency = 126 ÷ 14 = 9 units/day

⇒ A efficiency = 126 ÷ 63 = 2 units/day

⇒ B efficiency = 9 − 2 = 7 units/day

⇒ Half work = 126 ÷ 2 = 63 units

⇒ Time for B = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 days

**∴ B alone will take 9 days to do half of the work.**

questions.question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 8 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 9(1/3)​ hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by pump alone = 8 hours

Time taken by pump with leak = 9(1/3) = 28/3 hours

**Formula used:**

Work rate = 1 ÷ time

Leak rate = Pump rate − Combined rate

**Calculation:**

Let total work = LCM of 8 and 28 = 56 units

Pump rate = 56 ÷ 8 = 7 units/hour

Combined rate = 56 ÷ (28/3) = 56 × 3/28 = 6 units/hour

Leak rate = 7 − 6 = 1 unit/hour

Time for leak to empty full tank = 56 ÷ 1 = 56 hours

**∴ The leak will empty the full tank in 56 hours.**

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 14 days. If A alone can do it in 56 days, then B alone can do three-fourth of the same work in days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B can complete the work in 14 days

A alone can complete the work in 56 days

Find: Time taken by B alone to do 3/4 of the work

**Formula used:**

Work done per day = 1 ÷ Time

Work rate of B = (A + B rate) − A rate

**Calculation:**

Let total work = LCM of 14 and 56 = 56 units

A + B can do = 56 ÷ 14 = 4 units/day

A alone can do = 56 ÷ 56 = 1 unit/day

⇒ B alone can do = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day

3/4 of work = (3/4) × 56 = 42 units

Time taken by B = 42 ÷ 3 = 14 days

**∴ B alone can do 3/4 of the work in 14 days.**

Work rate = 1 / Time

⇒ B's 1 day work = (4 − 3) / 72 = 1/72

1/4 work ⇒ 72 × 1/4 = 18 days

**∴ B alone can do 1/4 work in 18 days.**

questions.question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 7½ hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
questions.solution:

Pump fills tank in 6 hours

Pump + leak fill tank in 7½ hours = 15/2 hours

Choose total work = LCM units

Rate = Work ÷ Time

Leak rate = Pump rate − Combined rate

Time to empty = Work ÷ Leak rate

**Calculation:**

⇒ Combined rate = 30 ÷ (15/2) = 30 × 2 ÷ 15 = 4 units/hour

⇒ Leak rate = 5 − 4 = 1 unit/hour

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 15 days. If A alone can do it in 17 days, then B alone can do two-third of the same work in _______ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together complete work in 15 days.

A alone = 17 days.

**Formula used:**

Total Work = LCM of (15, 17)

Work rate = Work ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

LCM(15, 17) = 255 units (Total Work)

Work rate of A+B = 255 ÷ 15 = 17 units/day

Work rate of A = 255 ÷ 17 = 15 units/day

Work rate of B = 17 - 15 = 2 units/day

B’s time for 2/3 work = (2/3 × 255) ÷ 2 = 170 ÷ 2 = 85 days

**∴ B alone can do two-third of the work in 85 days.**

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 3 hours and 36 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 4 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill two-third of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tap A fills in 3 hours

Tap B fills in 36 hours

Tap C empties in 4 hours

**Calculation:**

LCM of denominators 3, 36, 4 = 36 ⇒ total work = 36 units (1 cistern = 36 units)

⇒ Efficiency A = 36/3 = 12 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency B = 36/36 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Efficiency C = −36/4 = −9 units/hr (emptying)

⇒ Net efficiency = 12 + 1 − 9 = 4 units/hr

⇒ Work required = 2/3 of cistern = 2/3 × 36 = 24 units

⇒ Time = Work / Net efficiency = 24 / 4 = 6 hours

**∴ Time required = 6 hours.**

questions.question: Three water pipes m, n and p, take 5, 6 and 12 hours, respectively, to fill a water tank. If all three pipes are opened at the same time, then the required time to fill the water tank will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Times: m = 5 h, n = 6 h, p = 12 h

**Calculations:**

LCM(5,6,12) = 60 ⇒ Total work = 60 units

Efficiency of m = 60 ÷ 5 ⇒ 12 units/h

Efficiency of n = 60 ÷ 6 ⇒ 10 units/h

Efficiency of p = 60 ÷ 12 ⇒ 5 units/h

Combined efficiency = 12 + 10 + 5 ⇒ 27 units/h

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 27 = 20 ÷ 9 hours = 2(2)/(9) hours 

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 20 days. If A alone can do it in 45 days, then B alone can do one-third of the same work in _______ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B finish work in 20 days

A alone finishes in 45 days

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(20, 45) = 180 units

Efficiency(A + B) = 180 ÷ 20 = 9 units/day

Efficiency(A) = 180 ÷ 45 = 4 units/day

Efficiency(B) = 9 − 4 = 5 units/day

B’s one-third work = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 units

Time taken = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ B alone can do one-third of work in 12 days.**

questions.question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 4 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 9 (1)/(3) hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by pump to fill tank = 4 hrs

Time taken with leakage = 9¹/₃ hrs = 28/3 hrs

**Formula used:**

Work rates are added/subtracted.

LCM method is used for efficiency.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 4 and 28/3 = 28

Let total work = 28 units

Pump’s 1 hr work = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 units

Net 1 hr work (pump + leak) = 28 ÷ (28/3) = 3 units

⇒ Leak’s 1 hr work = 7 - 3 = 4 units (emptying)

Time taken by leak alone = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 hrs

**∴ Leak will empty the tank in 7 hours.**

questions.question: Three taps A, B and C together can fill an empty cistern in 20 minutes. Tap A alone can fill it in 50 minutes and tap B alone in 60 minutes. How long will tap C alone take to fill it (in minutes)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B + C can fill in 20 min

A alone = 50 min

B alone = 60 min

**Formula used:**

Work per min = 1 / Time

(A + B + C) work/min = A work/min + B work/min + C work/min

**Calculation:**

A work/min = 1/50

B work/min = 1/60

(A + B + C) work/min = 1/20

⇒ 1/20 = 1/50 + 1/60 + 1/C

⇒ 1/20 - (1/50 + 1/60) = 1/C

⇒ 1/20 - 11/300 = 1/C

⇒ (15 - 11)/300 = 1/C

⇒ 4/300 = 1/C

⇒ C = 75

**∴ Tap C alone will take 75 minutes.**

questions.question: There are two pumps to fill a tank with water. The first pump can fill the empty tank in 6 hours, while the second in 8 hours. If both the pumps are opened at the same time and kept open for 2 hours, the part of tank that will be filled up is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by the first pump to fill the tank = 6 hours.

Time taken by the second pump to fill the tank = 8 hours.

Time both pumps are open = 2 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Work done (part of the tank filled) = Efficiency × Time

Efficiency = 1 / Time taken to fill the tank

Total work done = Work done by Pump 1 + Work done by Pump 2

**Calculation:**

Efficiency of Pump 1 = 1 / 6

Efficiency of Pump 2 = 1 / 8

Total Efficiency = (1 / 6) + (1 / 8)

Total Efficiency = (4 + 3) / 24

Total Efficiency = 7 / 24

Work done in 2 hours = Total Efficiency × Time

Work done in 2 hours = (7 / 24) × 2

⇒ Work done = 14 / 24

⇒ Work done = 7 / 12

**The part of the tank filled in 2 hours is 7/12.**
